question: Can a shared Bayes LoRA FTN atom bank post-train sequential image domains, retain learned domains, and recover useful masks by the original mask inference machinery?
backbone: Official ImageNet pretrained SiT-XL/2 256x256; frozen; original class embeddings retained
data: Imagenette2-320, ten classes with original ImageNet labels
split_note: Disjoint original source images across train/support/test; same source-image identities paired across styles. Support/test come from Imagenette validation split.
targets: all 28 blocks: attention qkv/proj and MLP fc1/fc2
inference: Unchanged bayesian_adv/bayes_reconfig.py; 2 persistent updates, beta=1, T=3, Adam lr=.3; 30-step loss-triggered change-point refits; cold evaluation starts at zero, 30 steps, T=1, one restart, final deterministic top-k (take_best=False)

training.optimizer: Adam; reset moments per block as original runner
training.precision: bfloat16 autocast, float32 parameters and losses

budget_note: Increased planned 600 to original method's 1500 updates per block after GPU throughput benchmark, before substantive training; smoke uses only two updates per domain for API verification.

replay.mask: stored mask; updates all its active atoms

evaluations.rng: fixed paired noise, times and search seeds; evaluation restores training RNG and mask state
evaluations.generation: 20 images per domain/stage, fixed seeds/classes, Heun 50 steps, original CFG=4 implementation

runs: replay and no-replay paired at seeds 123/124/125
ordinary LoRA matched active rank at seed123
replay reversed domain order at seed123
optional_input_prior: Implemented fixed PCA keys on pooled clean latents and retrieved logits; direct/refine/fallback variants. Off for primary runs; evaluate diagnostically if cold recall fails.
limitations: Controlled synthetic style domains, not independent real-world domain corpora
Known block schedule resets optimizer but does not force mask boundaries
Frozen base recovery alone is not evidence of learned-domain retention
Velocity MSE and qualitative grids require generated-distribution checks for image-quality claims
Bank capacity and replay budget reduced from toy defaults for transformer compute; mechanism preserved
reporting: Report failures and negative results. Separate adaptation, atom retention, mask recovery, and prospective performance relative to each domain's initial baseline. No test examples or test-loss tuning in training or inference.
